evidence.excerpt:
As illustrated in Figure 1, SLICE-Mem separates online memory formation from offline consoli-
dation. Given a dialogueU= (u 1, . . . , uT ), with speaker, text, and timestamp for each turn, the
online pipeline admits informative user turns, extracts predicate-centered statements, and inserts
their embeddings with timestamp and provenance. Admission and extraction use a compact clas-
sifier and deterministic linguistic rules without generative LLM calls. Consolidation subsequently
reconciles relations among stored entries without rewriting their text.

evidence.excerpt:
After online memory construction, SLICE-Mem performs offline consolidation to identify redun-
dant or outdated information among stored entries [7, 22]. It updates entry statuses to guide sub-
sequent retrieval while preserving the original text, embeddings, and timestamps, without deleting
or rewriting memories.
The procedure begins with deterministic rules for clear duplicates and changes in mutually
exclusive personal attributes. Duplicate detection considers whether entries refer to the same
occurrence, so similar descriptions of separate events remain available. State changes are processed
in timestamp order, allowing a return to an earlier value to be retained as a new transition. For
entries that remain active, the system retrieves similar candidates whose message timestamps are no
later than the target's. A LLM then classifies the relation between the target and each

The four possible decisions areignore, which leaves the entries unchanged,dedup, which marks
the later duplicate as redundant,supersede, which marks the older entry as outdated and links it
to its replacement, andqualify, which records a compatible relation while retaining both entries.
Before applying a decision that would exclude an entry from ordinary retrieval, the system checks
the stated relation, its scope, and supporting text from the target. Unsupported decisions are
ignored. Additional checks enforce consistent status changes and replacement links. The prompt
also directs the model to retain complementary information and avoid replacing an entire entry

evidence.excerpt:
SLICE-Mem separates the cost of forming useful memories online from the cost and risks of later
reconciliation. Against the five baseline frameworks in Tables 1 and 2, the results show that
selective admission and deterministic extraction can preserve competitive downstream performance
with substantially fewer generative calls and tokens. They do not establish a universal runtime
advantage, and the total cost of a consolidated system must include its offline stage. Component
training and teacher annotation are additional preparation costs outside the reported operational
comparisons.
10
Consolidation is not uniformly beneficial. Status-based suppression can restrict retrieval of
useful historical evidence even when the original text remains stored. The Memora 30B and 8B
results differ, motivating policies that preserve complementary episodes and defer uncertain relation
decisions. The

evaluation measures downstream effectiveness and operational cost, but does not

The present pipeline admits only user turns, limiting coverage of assistant-authored evidence.
The one-annotator Gate audit and automatic extractor diagnostics at the deployedτ g = 0.2 do not
establish proposition-level factuality or complete coreference resolution. The fixed HanLP parser
and extraction rules have not been systematically stress-tested under domain shift, disfluency, or
controlled parser errors. The threshold is selected from a full nine-point end-to-end sweep on
Memora Weekly, also used for reporting. Exact-string de-duplication does not rule out semantic
overlap. Evaluation is limited to two dialogue-memory benchmarks, without heterogeneous-source
testing such as RHELM [34].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: A disjoint 150-turn human-annotated audit reports AUPRC 0.898 and 93.3% human-teacher agreement, corroborating the learned admission signal independently of the teacher supervision used for training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are downstream Memora Weekly FAMA and LongMemEval-S accuracy, graded by a fixed GPT-OSS-20B judge, with a separate human-annotated audit of gate decisions.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The Salience Gate is trained on consensus labels from three heterogeneous LLM teachers and released Memora admission annotations, with the operating threshold selected by an end-to-end FAMA sweep on Memora Weekly.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding efficiency gains (reducing LLM token consumption by over 90% online while retaining competitive answer accuracy) are well supported by the experimental data and ablations.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations on Memora Weekly and LongMemEval-S rigorously benchmark accuracy and token/runtime efficiency across 8B and 30B backbones against strong baselines (MemOS, A-MEM, LightMem). Component ablations and sensitivity checks are thoroughly provided.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: An independent audit on 150 human-annotated turns demonstrated 93.3% agreement and high AUPRC (0.898), corroborating gate precision independently of teacher supervision.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Downstream benchmark answer evaluations graded by a fixed GPT-OSS-20B judge on Memora Weekly FAMA and LongMemEval-S accuracy, plus an independent human audit of gate decisions.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Consensus labels from three heterogeneous LLM teachers (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.2, Kimi-K2.6) and released Memora training annotations trained the Salience Gate classifier.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently document limitations, including restriction to user turns, performance plateaus/drops from offline consolidation on certain tasks, lack of heterogeneous external document support, and reliance on proxy diagnostics.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the salience gate architecture, multi-teacher annotation distillation pipeline, deterministic semantic dependency parsing rules, and validation checks during consolidation.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled evaluation of an efficient long-term memory architecture with detailed ablations, honest discussion of negative or mixed consolidation impacts, and clear methodological documentation.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces SLICE-Mem, a lightweight LLM agent memory framework combining a learned salience classifier for online turn admission with deterministic dependency-based extraction, while offloading relation updates to offline consolidation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled evaluation of an efficient long-term memory architecture with detailed ablations, honest discussion of negative or mixed consolidation impacts, and clear methodological documentation.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently document limitations, including restriction to user turns, performance plateaus/drops from offline consolidation on certain tasks, lack of heterogeneous external document support, and reliance on proxy diagnostics.
